messages:
Anna: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel swap on canary we saw p99 jump ~2.4x during the EU cross-region fallback smoke tests :eyes:
Anna: Quick summary: swap happened 02:50 UTC, routing experiment forced ~30% traffic to fallback region. Baseline p99 ~120ms, spike to ~280ms. Attaching short profile excerpt below:
```
flame: (top) memcpy -> context_switch -> grpc_pollset_work -> kernel_dispatch
hotspots: kv_cache::lookup (30%), batching::enqueue_wait (22%), kernel_timers (15%)
```
Mike: Only when fallback activated? or also seen on normal local routing?
Anna: Primarily during fallback fanout. Local-only runs stayed ~baseline. The canary that had the new kernel + batch tweak was the only node group showing the spike.
Devon: Two quick hypotheses: 1) larger microbatch cap increased queueing for short requests (p95 stable, p99 widened) 2) cross-region fallback churn causes KV cache cold prefixes -> amplified misses when batches aggregate those requests -> extra work per-token
Sara: I profiled network/syscalls — saw increased recvmsg and epoll_wait wait times, and memcpy latency jumped on the canary. Snippet:
```
# perf top (summary)
  memcpy  18%
  context_switch 12%
  kv_cache::miss_handler 25%
```
Mike: Sounds like batching + kernel changes made context switch/memcopy path costlier under mixed-length workloads. Quick mitigation: reduce microbatch cap from 16 -> 6 on canary and throttle fallback routing to 10% while we debug.
Anna: Reverted the kernel on canary at 03:12 UTC to isolate — p99 dropped to ~160ms (better but not back to baseline). Suggests a combo effect.
Devon: I'll run a controlled experiment: simulated cross-region prefix churn with 10k reqs, vary microbatch cap [2,4,6,8,12,16], measure tail latency and kv miss amplification. Will also capture kernel syscalls.
Sara: Also propose a short-term server-side KV pre-warm for known-hot prefixes during fallback ramp to reduce cold-miss storms. Could be a background async prefetch triggered when route changes.
Mike: Agree on both. Ops suggestion: add an emergency routing policy: prefer local region until per-route kv_miss_rate < threshold OR until local CPU < 70%. That would avoid broad fallback during noisy kernel transitions.
Anna: Action items: 1) @Devon run microbatch sweep + upload traces (ETA 6h); 2) @Sara prototype KV pre-warm (ETA EOD); 3) @Mike and I add a fallback-safety throttle and dashboard panel for per-route kv_miss amplification (ETA tomorrow AM). I'll keep the canary reverted until experiments complete.
Devon: Starting the harness now. Will post CSV + flame links here.
ci-bot: Revert job finished: kernel-revert-canary #824 succeeded at 03:12 UTC :white_check_mark:
Anna: Thanks — keeping this thread for the debrief. If anyone sees another p99 blip while the canary is reverted please ping here with the trace id.
